name: OpenHands Software Agent SDK
summary: Builds and runs coding agents with conversations, tools, workspaces, events, and an agent server.
memoryUse: The agent server stores conversation metadata and JSON Lines event logs beside the project workspace.
fit: Useful for studying how coding-agent execution state and event history can be captured and resumed.
boundary: The repository describes an implementation surface; this entry does not claim a measured memory benefit.

name: SWE-agent
summary: Runs language-model agents on GitHub issues with repository tools, sandboxed execution, and trajectory inspection.
memoryUse: Its configuration and trajectory records make within-task context policies inspectable.
fit: A concrete harness for comparing context selection, observation masking, and summarization on repair tasks.
boundary: A harness may be used without durable cross-task memory; configuration does not by itself establish a memory effect.

name: mini-swe-agent
summary: Provides a compact software-engineering agent for GitHub issues and command-line work.
memoryUse: A small agent loop provides a baseline for adding and measuring context or persistent-memory components.
fit: Useful when an experiment needs a readable coding harness with fewer moving parts.
boundary: The repository is a harness, not an out-of-the-box cross-task memory system.

name: Aider
summary: Pairs with a developer in a repository and supplies a token-budgeted map of code symbols to the model.
memoryUse: The repository map selects code context; optional chat-history files can preserve prior conversation text.
fit: Useful for studying repository context selection and the difference between current code maps and retained history.
boundary: A repository map is code context, not automatically a verified record of past decisions or experience.

name: Cline
summary: Offers an autonomous coding agent through an IDE extension, CLI, and SDK.
memoryUse: Can serve as a coding environment for comparing an external MCP memory layer with ordinary task context.
fit: Useful where a memory method needs a real developer-facing coding agent and an extensible tool interface.
boundary: Compatibility with a memory service is a proposed research fit, not a tested pairing in this atlas.

name: Letta Code
summary: Runs stateful agents with persistent memory, message search, and agent-owned skills.
memoryUse: Its MemFS stores versioned context and skills in a git-backed memory repository.
fit: A direct case for examining cross-session continuity and mutable skill memory in a coding harness.
boundary: Repository documentation describes capabilities; the atlas has not independently benchmarked them.

name: Mem0
summary: Provides a reusable persistent-memory layer for AI agents and applications.
memoryUse: Stores agent and user facts for retrieval across interactions.
fit: A candidate memory layer for testing whether a coding agent retrieves and follows prior project or user facts.
boundary: The linked repository is general-purpose; software-development outcomes need a separate evaluation.

name: Graphiti
summary: Builds temporal knowledge graphs from agent episodes and changing data.
memoryUse: Facts carry valid and invalid times, allowing newer information to supersede older graph relationships.
fit: A candidate backend for testing stale repository facts and time-aware project knowledge.
boundary: The repository is not itself evidence that temporal graphs improve completed code repairs.

name: Cognee
summary: Turns documents, code, and conversations into searchable graph and vector memory for agents.
memoryUse: Exposes remember, recall, improve, and forget operations, with coding-agent integrations described in its repository.
fit: A candidate memory substrate for comparing codebase knowledge retrieval and memory maintenance.
boundary: General product claims and repository examples are not matched coding-task comparisons in this atlas.

name: Basic Memory
summary: Offers local-first Markdown knowledge management with MCP, CLI, and API interfaces.
memoryUse: Keeps human-readable notes and links indexed locally for an agent to read and update.
fit: A candidate for comparing inspectable project notes with structured records in coding workflows.
boundary: Its repository does not establish a controlled software-repair benefit.

name: MCP Memory Service
summary: Exposes persistent semantic memory to AI agents and coding assistants through MCP and HTTP interfaces.
memoryUse: Supports storage, retrieval, and consolidation with local vector search and selectable backends.
fit: A candidate adapter for testing persistent memory across coding sessions and clients.
boundary: The described interfaces do not establish improved coding quality without a matched evaluation.
